en.faq_about_desc:
Varlet Crash Diagnostic is an {{'open source' link=repo}} tool made by {{'alxl' link=alxl}} to help users find the most relevant information for what caused Darktide to crash.

By grabbing only the relevant information from your console logs, you will be able to help yourself more easily when you run into issues. If you seek help from other people, you can save them some time by giving them only the information they'd go looking for in the console log anyway.
en.faq_log_location_desc: The directory that contains your console logs is different per platform.
en.faq_upload_title: My browser is warning me against uploading files. Is this safe?
en.faq_upload_desc:
Rest assured that this tool does not actually upload any files; all of the processing is done entirely on your own machine, and it never sends any information of any kind to any server.

You don't have to take my word for it! Here's the {{'source code' link=repo}}. You can run it locally, if you like.
en.input_paste_desc: The crash message usually isn't enough to diagnose an issue. Console logs are far more informative. Specify the console log directory; see above for how to find it.
en.input_file_desc: Make sure the console log you select is the log created during the session that ended in a crash. A new console log is created every time the game is launched, not when it crashes or closes. See above for console log location.
en.report_desc: If you are seeking help from others, use the options below to send this report to them.
en.report_text_desc: As the report is obnoxiously long, you should try to send it as a file if you can. Only send the text on its own if sharing the file is not possible.
en.insight_dxgi_desc: This is a GPU crash, which is a problem with the base game. Some people have reported success in rolling back to older drivers. Other potential fixes can be found here: {{link=dxgi}}
en.insight_oom_desc:
This is a crash caused by the Lua heap running out of space. Note that this is not related to your entire system's RAM. This is probably caused by some reckless memory allocation by a mod.

You can increase the heap size to a maximum of 2048 by adding `--lua-heap-mb-size 2048` to your launch options or by editing a config file: {{link=oom}}
en.insight_dml_desc:
Make sure DML is up-to-date and installed correctly.
{{link=dml}}
en.insight_dmf_desc:
Make sure DMF is up-to-date and installed correctly.
{{link=dmf}}
en.insight_crash_message_desc_lone: {{modName}} is named in the crash message; it's a very likely culprit.
en.insight_crash_message_desc_input: {{modName}} is named in the crash message; however, this error may be caused by a mod that affects inputs earlier in the load order.
en.insight_dmlf_loaded_twice_title: Do not include DMF or base in your load order file
en.insight_dmlf_loaded_twice_desc: Do not include dmf or base in your load order file. Those get loaded automatically.
en.insight_duplicate_mods_desc: The following mod(s) are listed more than once in your load order: {{dupes}}
en.insight_no_crash_desc: This log does not appear to contain a crash. A new console log is created every time the game launches, not when it closes or crashes.
en.insight_ui_info_desc:
This looks like a UI-related crash. To help you identify the bugged mod, here's some information possibly related to the part of the UI causing the problem:
{{uiInfoList}}
en.insight_lua_stack_title: Mods named in the Lua stack
en.insight_lua_stack_desc: The following mod(s) are named in the stack, indicating that they are potential culprits: {{modNames}}
en.insight_hook_chain_desc_solid_only:
The following mods hooked functions with the same name as those involved in the callstack. This could identify a culprit, or reveal a mod incompatibility, or mean absolutely nothing.
{{solid}}
en.insight_none_desc_paste: Specify the console log directory above to get more information.
en.insight_none_desc_file: Your best bet is to look at the callstack to get an idea of what the game was doing when it crashed, then disabling mods that you think may be related to that. If all else fails, you can try disabling half of your mods at a time to narrow down the culprit.
en.hint_no_uploads: Note: no files are actually uploaded.
